content:
Earlier in June, we already reported that three Russian banks under U.S. sanctions managed to bypass review and successfully get their client apps on the App Store. Two months later, another case has climbed to the top of the iPhone App Store.

This time, the protagonist is K8CHEN PRO. The App Store description packages it as an application that uses augmented reality (AR) to design kitchens.

But as soon as you open the app, the fake shell immediately falls apart. The privacy policy linked on the App Store turns out to have been generated by a "Free Privacy Policy Generator," which is already alarming enough on its own.

Regardless, this app is clearly the client app for T-Bank. What interests me is that apps like these keep passing Apple's review.

When these apps attract enough attention and climb the App Store rankings, anyone can see at a glance that they have no business being there. This situation is truly puzzling.

The other cases from June can be found here and here.

Update: As expected, the app has already been removed from the App Store.
